messages.subject: Re: SECR when sampling grids are larger than the HR
messages.subject_clean: SECR when sampling grids are larger than the HR
messages.body_plain:
If I'm understanding right then you can divide each 4-km square into say 4 2-km squares and treat each as a point (proximity) detector. That should give enough spatial resolution, but you also have the option of 1-km squares. Perhaps input the 4-km squares as polygon detectors and use secr::discretize?

> I'm sorry if this wasn't clear. We laid down 4km x 4km grids over the entire study area (over 100 grids) and scanned each grid for scats. We do have the location of each scat.
>

> > Can you please clarify: a search for scats was conducted over a large area, and the only location data for each scat is the 4-km x 4-km grid square in which it was found? This doesn't seem to provide sufficient spatial resolution. But maybe I'm misunderstanding.
> > Murray
> > On Friday, May 30, 2025 at 11:18:55 AM UTC+12 tashi...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > Hello Efford and others,
> > >
> > > I have data on individual captures and recaptures for a species from a scat survey and intend to estimate density. The grid size used to collect the scats was 4km x 4km, but the species has a home range of less than 5 sq km. I was going to use each grid as a detector.

messages.subject: secr 5.2.4 etc.
messages.body_plain:
Three packages were updated last week.
secr <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=secr> 5.2.4 has mostly minor changes <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/secr/NEWS>. Simulation of activity centres with sim.popn() allows fixed-N when model2D uses rLGCP or rThomas, building on changes in the spatstat package.
secrdesign <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=secrdesign> 2.10.0 adds functions to simulate movement paths from an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (simOU), and hence to simulate detections at point detectors that are serially correlated in space (simOU.capthist). These functions are exercised in the vignette available here <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secrdesign-vignette.pdf>.
ipsecr <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ipsecr> 1.4.4 is most interesting for a new example in the vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ipsecr/vignettes/ipsecr-vignette.pdf> that implements an idea from Kodi et al. (2024 MEE 15:1060-1070) for reducing bias due to identification errors.

messages.subject: Error while trying to run single session secr for leopard camera trap data
messages.subject_clean: Error while trying to run single session secr for leopard camera trap data
messages.body_plain:
Good morning everybody

I have been trying to run secr analysis on my leopard camera trap data, and keep getting the following error

"Error in read.traps(file = "trapfile.csv", detector = "count", skip = 0, : 'usage' fields suggest varying number of occasions"

Could anyone help? I cant seem to find the error in the data, and neither can chatgpt.

Happy to send my csv files and code to see if anyone can find the error

messages.subject_clean: Error while trying to run single session secr for leopard camera trap data
messages.body_plain:
Hard to say without the data, but I'm guessing that a leading zero in a string of binary codes has been helpfully dropped by Excel or R. You will need to find a workaround e.g. place the usage code for each occasion in a separate column of the csv file.
Murray
